title: Weights in the Fish
narrativeQuestion: How did two anglers rig a Lake Erie championship, how were they caught, and was the payoff worth what it cost them?

chapters.title: The Scale
chapters.claim: Runyan and Cominsky's five walleye weighed 33.91 pounds at the September 30, 2022 LEWT championship in Cleveland.

chapters.title: Nobody Could Beat Them
chapters.claim: The team won 9 of the 19 events Jason Fischer ran from 2019, against 2 for the next best team, after a 2021 polygraph disqualification and a 2022 Rossford investigation.

namedPeople.name: Jason Fischer
namedPeople.role: Lake Erie Walleye Trail tournament director

chapters.title: Five Pound Cookie Cutters
chapters.claim: Fischer judged the fish to look like ordinary four to five pound walleye, cut them open and found lead sinkers and fillets while the crowd filmed.

chapters.title: Pull the Lead Out
chapters.claim: Ten sinkers weighed 7 pounds. Without them the bag drops to 26.91 pounds, below the 28.18 pound leader.

chapters.title: From the Ramp to Jail
chapters.claim: The pair were indicted, pleaded guilty to cheating and unlawful ownership of wild animals, and were sentenced on May 11, 2023.

chapters.title: Was It Worth It?
chapters.claim: They chased $28,760 and lost a $100,000 boat, three years of fishing, ten days of freedom and a clean record.

accuracyNotes: Sinker total uses the court affidavit figures of eight 12 ounce and two 8 ounce weights, exactly 7 pounds. NPR reported 7.58 pounds. The page uses the affidavit figure.
The weight of the stuffed fillets was never published, so the page says the de-leaded total is still too high.
The win grid shows counts only. The order of individual wins across the 19 events is not shown because it is not in the record.
